decision.prompt: A checkpoint reveals that joint marks are taken from different datums. What is the strongest response?
options: Pause at a safe point, correct the cause of joint marks are taken from different datums, then repeat the specified checks before continuing.
Continue and hide the issue during finishing.
Change the drawing or specification to match the work.
Leave it for the next trade without recording it.
decision.feedback: Correct the rod before any timber is marked or machined from it.

commonFaults: joint marks are taken from different datums
a finished size is confused with a cutting size
the rod lacks reference-face marks

questions.prompt: Why is “Select a straight stable rod and establish datum” important on this task?
questions.guide: One datum prevents cumulative errors as details are transferred to components.

questions.prompt: How would you check that this work meets the drawing or specification?
questions.guide: Reconcile overall and chain dimensions, then check joints from the same face and edge.

questions.prompt: What would you do if joint marks are taken from different datums?
questions.guide: Correct the rod before any timber is marked or machined from it.
